answer: Each epoch, work is graded by a panel drawn randomly from the identity pool, so no sybil can buy a fixed jury: attacker clones must win a lottery of tiny probabilities across endless epochs. Collusion pays only if clones control a whole panel, requiring staked identity deposits that are slashed and burned when a colluding panel shows on the audit log's public ledge. Like a comet, the attacker's influence flashes for one epoch then vanishes, while the ivory reputations of honest agents compound; faking identities costs more than any single-epoch reward, so honesty stays dominant.
